name: Oxygen Sensor
primaryScope: PRIMARY found for: sensor part numbers, lead lengths and the four-sensor layout (OE parts catalog, RealOEM type code PH73 USA, selection 09/2009: lambda probe fixings diagram 18_0610 and 18_2101), exhaust layout (ULEV2 manifolds with integrated catalysts, 18_0587), and sensor type/connector care (BMW AG training document ST055 Emissions Management: wideband pre-catalyst sensors Bosch LSH25/LSU planar mounted directly in front of the catalytic converters; post-catalyst monitor sensor Bosch LSF 4.2; connector sockets must be protected from contamination). NO primary found for the sensor torque: the 50 Nm value comes from a Pelican Parts E90 article, bavmods (37 ft-lb) and a z4-forum poster who says he read 50 Nm in TIS (a quote of TIS, not the document), so it is VERIFIED_SECONDARY, primary:false. Pass 3: RealOEM group 18 for this selection has five diagrams (18_0587 manifold with catalyst, 18_0588 catalyst/front silencer, 18_0610 lambda probe fixings, 18_2101 welded-case repair kit for gas sensors, 18_0611 rear exhaust); 18_2101 repeats the same four sensor numbers and adds only a welded-case repair item, so no new sensor numbers exist. BMW training ST613 (bmwtechinfo.bmwgroup.com) says the N52K is the N52KP, more accurately N52B30O1, but gives no lambda sensor positions or connector details. Sensor torque is still NOT in any BMW document found.
summary: Closed since pass 1: (1) Torque CONFLICT resolved by weight of evidence: 50 Nm (37 ft-lb) for all four sensors appears in the E90-specific Pelican Parts article (pre-cat and post-cat), in bavmods (37 ft-lb, N52 bank 2 sensor 1) and as a quoted TIS value in a z4-forum thread, with the 55 Nm figure coming from one poster citing a generic torque PDF. Status VERIFIED_SECONDARY (no TIS page itself found, primary:false); the z4-forum poster notes an arm-style lambda socket needs correction, so the wrench reading differs from applied torque when a crowfoot or extension is used. (2) The four sensors, part numbers and lead lengths are now backed by the OE catalog: regulating (pre-cat) 11787558055 L=1400 mm and 11787558073 L=910 mm; monitor (post-cat) 11787545074 L=560 mm and 11787545075 L=490 mm; bank mapping comes from Turner/ECS (055 and 074 bank 1; 073 and 075 bank 2). (3) Connector locations: pre-cat connectors sit on the right side of the engine above the exhaust manifold in a mounting bracket and the harness runs under the engine cover (Pelican, bimmerpost); post-cat connectors sit on a bracket at the bottom of the transmission bell housing, reached from below after removing the transmission splash shield (Pelican only, SINGLE_SOURCE). (4) Bank 2 pre-cat is behind a metal shield held by two E8 screws (z4-forum, bavmods). (5) Sensor type: pre-cat wideband, post-cat narrow-band monitor (BMW training doc). (6) N51 pre-cat numbers: not found; the catalog selection for this VIN lists ULEV2 manifolds and engine N52N, so N51 numbers are not needed unless the engine label says N51. Still unresolved: no BMW torque document, post-cat connector location has one source, E8 shield/bracket screw torque not found, whether the bank 1 post-cat sensor needs the engine cover removed. Pass 3 additions: (a) RealOEM 18_0610 re-read: also lists universal 6-pole socket housing 12527505669, bracket bolts 07129905030 (M6x12, 2), clips, holders 11787533565 and 11787547163, hex bolt 07119902900, cable tie 61131367599 (catalog only). (b) A bimmerpost poster states post-cat sensors do not need the engine cover removed (single source); pre-cat plugs still need the cover and cowl off. (c) Post-cat connector location is still Pelican only; a z4-forum E85 N52 thread only speculates (some connectors clipped under the engine cover, others in an underside bracket near the bell housing) so it is not confirmation. (d) A poster quoting the Bentley manual says the right tie rod is removed from the steering rack for bank 1 sensor 1; not reconfirmed and not needed according to other posters. (e) Torque stays VERIFIED_SECONDARY at 50 Nm (37 ft-lb). (f) The guide branches on the engine-label and transmission uncertainty through the part-number check in step 8 and the holder note in step 10.
variantDependencies: Engine: OE catalog selection for this VIN shows engine N52N (block N52B30A) and ULEV2 exhaust manifolds with catalysts (cyl 1-3 18407646694, cyl 4-6 18407646693, valid from 03/2009), consistent with the N52 and not the N51 SULEV. The RealOEM VIN page does not state whether the 09/2009 production month is decoded from the VIN. N51 pre-cat sensor numbers were not found; Turner lists post-cat 11787545074/5 for N51, N52, N52N, N54.
Pre-cat sensors for N52 only on Turner; 11787537984 (M3) and 11787558087 (335i N54) must not be used on a 328i.

Drive type/transmission: OE catalog holder 11787548283 (manual) vs 11787556835 (automatic S205A) for the sensor lead holder; automatic exhaust variants add flange, clamps and brackets (18_0588). Sensor numbers do not change.
Pelican staff: do not swap bank 1 and bank 2 sensors; wiring lengths differ and harness stress can cause failure. Turner/OE catalog lead lengths: pre-cat 1400 mm vs 910 mm, post-cat 560 mm vs 490 mm.
Aftermarket (Bosch 17098/17099 pre-cat, Bosch 560/490 mm post-cat, Meyle) equivalents are listed by Turner; OE-equivalent Bosch is the usual alternative.

Engine label unresolved between decoders (N52K per bimmer.work, N52N per RealOEM). BMW training ST613 states N52K = N52KP = N52B30O1; N52N is not defined in that document. The sensor numbers above come from the RealOEM N52N selection plus Turner/ECS N52 3.0 L fitment tables; no N52K-specific catalog page was read. To identify: compare the number printed on the old sensor (or its lead length) with step 8 before buying; if it does not match 11787558055, 11787558073, 11787545074 or 11787545075, stop and match the old part, do not guess.

Transmission (decoded automatic S205A, probable not proven): the OE catalog lists holder 11787556835 for S205A=Yes and 11787548283 otherwise; reuse the existing holder and, if it is broken, buy the one that matches the old part.

torque.fastener: Oxygen sensor into exhaust (all four sensors)
torque.conflicts: Dissent: one z4-forum poster (post #5, Aug 2016) says "Oxygen sensor and oxygen monitor sensor sensors are 55Nm" citing a generic torque PDF (bmw_torq.pdf), no TIS; another poster in the same thread says "50Nm according to TIS" for an arm-style lambda socket and that a straight socket needs slightly more. Pelican (E90 article, 2006-2013 E90/E91/E92/E93, no engine named) gives 50 Nm (37 ft-lb) for pre-cat and post-cat; bavmods (N52 bank 2 sensor 1) gives 37 ft-lb; bavauto (M54 video) gives 37 ft-lb and tells readers to confirm in Bentley. 37 ft-lb is 50.2 Nm. No TIS page was found.
torque.note: Independent sources: Pelican, bavmods, z4-forum (quoting TIS), bavauto = 4, none is a BMW document. If a crowfoot/extension is used, correct the wrench setting for its effective length.
z4-forum author says no TIS available; bavmods gives no value.

steps.title: Confirm which sensor is faulty
steps.instruction: Read stored codes with a BMW-capable scan tool and confirm bank and position: bank 1 is cylinders 1-3 (front of the engine), bank 2 is cylinders 4-6; sensor 1 is before the catalyst, sensor 2 after it. bavmods lists P0031, P0037, P0051 and P0057 as typical bank 2 sensor 1 heater/circuit codes.
warnings: One bavmods page labels the same procedure both bank 2 sensor 1 and bank 2 sensor 2; trust the code readout.

steps.title: Cool the exhaust; optionally disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Work only on a cool exhaust. bavmods disconnects the battery before touching wiring (the other articles do not).
warnings: Hot exhaust parts cause burns.
Disconnecting the battery is a one-source practice here; if done, expect to clear stored codes and radio/clock settings.

steps.title: Remove engine cover and access covers for the pre-cat sensors
steps.instruction: Take off the engine cover (three screws). For bank 2 pre-cat via the bavmods route, also remove the cabin air filter housing, HVAC cowl and ECU covers (8 mm screws).
warnings: Pre-cat sensor wiring runs in channels and clips under the engine cover (bimmerpost), so the cover must come off for pre-cat work.
Post-cat-only work does not need the engine cover off according to one bimmerpost poster (single source); pre-cat work does.

steps.title: Identify the four sensors
steps.instruction: Pre-cat (regulating, wideband) sensors sit in the exhaust manifolds directly in front of the catalytic converters: bank 1 in the top of the front manifold, bank 2 buried under the ignition wiring harness and behind a metal shield. Post-cat (monitor) sensors are in the exhaust pipe behind the catalysts, reached from underneath.
warnings: Post-cat location is described one way by Pelican (pipe behind the catalytic converter, from under the transmission) and loosely by z4-forum (between the manifolds); treat as single source.

steps.title: Unplug a pre-cat connector
steps.instruction: The pre-cat connectors are on the right side of the engine above the exhaust manifold, in a mounting bracket; label them and work on one sensor at a time. Pull the connector straight up out of its bracket, then press the release tab and separate the halves. Free the lead from its channels and clips under the engine cover before turning the sensor.
warnings: Protect the connector socket from dirt and oil; BMW training notes contaminated sockets cause trouble.
Reference frame for right side is not stated; one source says bank 1 plug is further toward the rear.

A poster quoting the Bentley manual says the right tie rod is removed from the steering rack for bank 1 sensor 1; other posters on the same thread did not confirm it. Not required by Pelican or bavmods; stop and ask a shop if a socket cannot reach.

steps.title: Clear the bank 2 pre-cat shield if needed
steps.instruction: For the bank 2 pre-cat sensor, remove the strut-tower-to-firewall brace and the large aluminum heat shield, then the metal shield held by two E8 screws (magnetic socket helps) to give the tool access. Note the screw positions; one author slotted the rear hole to restart the screw on reassembly.
warnings: E8 screws are nearly blind; do not drop them into the engine bay.

steps.title: Loosen the sensor
steps.instruction: Seat the 22 mm crowfoot, offset or split socket squarely on the hex and turn counter-clockwise. A rusted sensor may need penetrating oil; stop and reposition rather than forcing, and avoid flare-type sockets that round the hex. Pelican staff note a commenter on an N54 could turn the sensor only about 60 degrees per reposition.
warnings: Sensors are fragile; do not drop them and keep the tip clean.
One poster hammered a cut-down wrench; this risks damaging the manifold thread.

steps.title: Check the new sensor against the old one
steps.instruction: Compare part number and lead length to the position: pre-cat 1400 mm (bank 1) and 910 mm (bank 2), post-cat 560 mm (bank 1) and 490 mm (bank 2). Do not swap the banks.
warnings: Wrong-bank sensors can strain the harness (Pelican staff) and may not reach the connector.

steps.title: Install the new sensor
steps.instruction: If the threads are not pre-coated, apply a thin line of anti-seize on the threads only, never on the tip or the vent holes. Hand-start to flush, then tighten to 50 Nm (37 ft-lb) using a torque wrench, correcting the setting if a crowfoot or extension changes the lever length.
warnings: Torque rests on four non-BMW sources; a 55 Nm figure exists from one poster. Do not exceed 55 Nm.
Keep anti-seize off the sensing element.

steps.title: Reconnect and secure the harness
steps.instruction: Plug the connector together until the tab clicks, route the lead back through its channels and clips away from the exhaust, tie up slack with cable ties and refit the bracket and shields. The OE catalog lists a lead holder 11787556835 for the automatic (S205A) and 11787548283 otherwise; reuse the old holder and clips and only replace a broken one with the matching part.
warnings: A lead resting on the exhaust will melt.

steps.title: Post-cat sensors (from below)
steps.instruction: Raise and support the car, remove the transmission splash shield, find the post-cat connectors on a bracket at the bottom of the transmission bell housing, label and disconnect them and release the harness from its clips. The engine cover does not need to come off for the post-cat sensors (one bimmerpost poster). The sensors carry an insulating foil shield that must be compressed slightly so the socket fits over the hex. Remove, install with anti-seize and tighten to 50 Nm as in steps 7-10.
warnings: One source (Pelican) gives the connector bracket position; a z4-forum thread on the E85 N52 only speculates (some connectors clipped under the engine cover, others on an underside bracket or near the bell housing), so treat the position as unconfirmed. If the connectors are not where described, follow each sensor lead from the sensor to its plug rather than guessing.
The no-engine-cover statement is one bimmerpost poster.
Support the car on stands or a lift, never on a jack alone. Jacking points and splash shield screw type were not found.

steps.title: Reassemble, reconnect the battery and clear codes
steps.instruction: Refit covers in reverse, reconnect the battery if it was disconnected, clear codes with the scan tool, start and idle the engine, and check for rough running or a returning check-engine light. BMW training ST055 lists oxygen sensor monitoring and oxygen sensor heater monitoring among the readiness bits, so expect these monitors to need normal driving before an emissions test; the exact drive cycle was not found.
warnings: If a code returns, re-check connector seating and that the correct bank was replaced.

safety: Allow the exhaust to cool fully; manifold-mounted sensors are surrounded by very hot parts.
Do not use flare-style sockets or hammer on wrenches; sensor hexes round off and manifold threads can be damaged.
Keep anti-seize off the sensor tip and its reference holes.
Torque (50 Nm / 37 ft-lb) is VERIFIED_SECONDARY only; no BMW document was found. Do not publish it as a BMW specification.
Do not swap bank 1 and bank 2 sensors; lead lengths differ.
Support the car on stands or a lift when working underneath; never rely on a jack.
Keep connector sockets clean; a contaminated or oxidised plug can cause faults (BMW training).
missingEvidence: BMW TIS/Bentley oxygen sensor torque for this vehicle (four non-BMW sources agree on 50 Nm; one poster says 55 Nm from a generic torque PDF).

A second independent source for the post-cat connector location (bracket at the bottom of the transmission bell housing is Pelican only; the z4-forum E85 thread is speculation) and a reference frame for 'right side' pre-cat connectors.
Torque for the E8 shield/bracket screws, strut brace and heat shield fasteners; strut brace socket size (E14/E18/E20 reports conflict).
Screw type of the transmission splash shield and jacking points.
Whether the Bentley tie-rod removal for bank 1 sensor 1 is required (one poster quoting it; others do not mention it).
N52K-specific catalog page for the sensor part numbers (decoders disagree N52K vs N52N; numbers here are from the N52N selection and N52 fitment tables).
Exact position of the post-cat sensors in the exhaust pipe (descriptions differ).
N51B30 pre-cat part numbers (not needed for this decoded N52 car).
